subject: Request: CloudBridge pilot - private offer / tiered discount approval
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudBridge pilot - request for private offer / tiered discount

Hi team,

I'm kicking off an approval request for a CloudBridge pilot that just moved from POC to 'pilot commercial' stage. They want to ship an AWS Marketplace private offer and asked for a tiered discount for the first 12 months. High-level:

- ARR run-rate for pilot year (estimated): $420k
- Expected first-year spend (pilot customers + expansion): $180k
- Requested discount: 30% off our list price for the first 12 months (private offer) to make the economics work for CloudBridge's procurement.
- Co-sell: CloudBridge is engaged with an AWS AE (Amy Park) who is willing to co-sell; they expect joint leads if we list a private offer rapidly.

Attached: short SOW, GTM summary and SKU export.

Why I think we should approve:
- Strategic: CloudBridge is a later-stage MSP with a strong vertical in fintech; demo to two credit unions already scheduled for Q4.
- Motion lift: AWS AE is lined up to push the private offer to two named accounts, increasing reach and ARR potential.
- Timing: CloudBridge asked for signed private offer by 9/03 to meet procurement window.

Ask: Can we approve a 30% private-offer discount for 12 months, but limit to pilot SKUs (see SKU file) and require a revenue minimum of $75k committed? If 30% is a hard no, what's the maximum concession we can sign off without deal desk escalation?

Thanks,
Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive, North America
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- CloudBridge_MAR_2027_PoC_SOW.pdf (application/pdf)
- CloudBridge_GTM_Summary.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
- CloudBridge_SKU_List.csv (text/csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudBridge pilot - request for private offer / tiered discount

Diego —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. A few quick clarifying Qs before I + Ben weigh in:

1) What's the current list price for the SKUs in the export? Need to see post-discount margin.
2) Is the $75k minimum commit flexible? Procurement usually counters on term/commit.
3) Can Amy (AWS AE) confirm co-sell incentive eligibility (SPL/offer must be published as private and have co-sell confirmation)?

If we can't justify 30% discount at the SKU level, propose alternative: 20% for first 6 months + additional 10% rebate if they hit $200k billing in year 1. Ben — can you run a quick margin sim?

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Diego —

Ran the SKU-level sim off Diego's CSV. Short answers:

- 30% across-the-board would push gross margin on those SKUs below our 45% target (on an average blended basis) and would be a no-go without offsetting funds.
- A 20% upfront private-offer discount for 6 months, then 10% ongoing for another 6, lands us near a 48% blended margin if we cap at $250k of billed ARR for the pilot year.
- If we attach a co-sell commit (AWS-confirmed joint pipeline + named-account coverage), we can seek a Marketplace listing credit from AWS (we should loop Amy) to make the 30% palatable.

Requesting the following to make an exception:
1) A signed minimum revenue commitment of $100k (rather than $75k) or a clawback clause if they underperform.
2) AWS AE (Amy) to confirm co-sell credit availability in writing (screenshot/link to private-offer confirmation is fine).
3) Legal to accept a 12-month private-offer with performance-based rebate language.

Stephanie — can you flag finance to pre-approve a one-time partner credit up to $30k if AWS can't provide a marketplace credit?

-Ben
Head of Marketplace Programs
Redwood Inference

Hi all — Amy from AWS. Quick confirmation: AWS can support a co-sell private offer and provide go-to-market credits on a case-by-case basis, but that requires the AWS AE to file a co-sell review and demonstrate named account engagement.

For CloudBridge: if you can provide the two named accounts and a short GTM plan (sales plays and expected touchpoints) I can start the Co-Sell Enablement request. AWS credits are not guaranteed but often approved for pilots demonstrating clear joint pipeline.

I've dropped a stub private-offer link below (you'll need seller account access to view).
